correctness.summary: Prime factors of phi(n) are stored in an int* buffer via (int)p / (int)tmp. When phi(n) has a prime factor exceeding int.MaxValue (2^31-1), the cast truncates it (often to a negative value), so phi/factors[i] yields a wrong (e.g. negative) exponent. ModPow with a non-positive exponent returns 1 because its `while (e>0)` loop never executes, making the order test `PowMod(g,exp,n)==1` always true; every candidate g is rejected and Run returns -1, failing to find a primitive root that actually exists.
correctness.triggeringInput: n = 4294967387 (a prime; phi(n)=n-1=2*2147483693 where the prime factor 2147483693 > int.MaxValue). Run returns -1 even though g=2 is a valid primitive root.
correctness.rootCause: `int* factors = stackalloc int[64];` plus `factors[fc++] = (int)p;` and `if (tmp > 1) factors[fc++] = (int)tmp;` narrow a long prime factor to int. For factors > 2^31-1 this overflows/becomes negative, then `phi / factors[i]` produces a wrong exponent and ModPow(g, negativeExp, n) returns 1 unconditionally (its loop guard is `while (e > 0)`).
correctness.suggestedFix: Store factors as long: declare `long* factors = stackalloc long[64];` and use `factors[fc++] = p;` / `factors[fc++] = tmp;` (remove the (int) casts). This keeps full-range prime factors so `phi / factors[i]` and the subsequent PowMod test are correct for all long n.

perf.summary: The candidate-root search calls Gcd(g,n) for every g and only then tests; for prime n the gcd is always 1 (wasted work), and PowMod exponents phi/factors[i] are recomputed in the inner loop instead of precomputed once.
perf.currentCost: Per candidate g: a full Euclid gcd, then up to fc PowMod (modular exponentiation, O(log e) mults each). phi/factors[i] divisions recomputed for every g though they are loop-invariant in g.
perf.proposedChange: Precompute long* exps = stackalloc long[fc] once: exps[i]=phi/factors[i] before the g-loop. Skip the Gcd call when n is known prime (Phi.Run(n)==n-1 implies n prime, gcd(g,n)==1 for all g<n). Inside g-loop reuse exps[i] in PowMod.
perf.rationale: Hoists fc divisions out of the O(n) candidate loop and eliminates a redundant gcd per candidate in the common prime-modulus case, cutting the per-candidate cost to just the PowMod tests.
perf.risk: The prime-detection shortcut (phi==n-1) is valid only for prime n; for composite n with primitive roots (n=2,4,p^k,2p^k) gcd must still be checked, so guard the skip with the phi==n-1 condition. exps array adds 64*8 bytes stack — within budget.

perf.summary: Private Gcd and PowMod wrappers duplicate functionality that exists elsewhere (ModPow.Run is already delegated to); Gcd could reuse a shared NT Gcd and be AggressiveInlined.
perf.currentCost: Local Gcd is a non-inlined static call per candidate; PowMod is a thin forwarding wrapper adding a call frame.
perf.proposedChange: Tag Gcd with [MethodImpl(MethodImplOptions.AggressiveInlining)] (and inline PowMod's body or mark it inlining) so the branchy abs+loop folds into the caller; or delegate to an existing shared Gcd in the NT module for consistency.
perf.rationale: Removes call overhead in the hot candidate loop and improves consistency/discoverability across the module. Branchless abs (mask = a>>63; a=(a^mask)-mask) further removes two branches but inputs g,n here are positive so the abs is dead — could drop the sign checks entirely in Run's call path.
perf.risk: g and n are always positive in Run, so the a<0/b<0 guards never fire; removing them in a Run-private fast path is safe only if Gcd is not reused with negative args elsewhere. Keep the public/general Gcd intact if shared.
